title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 'Longue Marche' circle of notes. L is a finitely generated field extension of K, of transcendence degree n. L̄ is an algebraic closure of L, which fixes a geometric generic point. A 'model' U is a regular scheme of finite type over K with function field L; X is a regular compactification of U. For any such scheme Y, E_Y^{L̄} denotes the fundamental group π_1(Y, Spec L̄). It is an extension of Gal(K̄/K) by the geometric fundamental group Π_{Y/K} = π_1(Y ⊗ K̄). The field case is E_L^{L̄} = Gal(L̄/L).

Formula (23) continues the previous page. Write U = X \ Z. Let D_i be the codimension-1 components of Z, x_i their generic points, and I_{x_i} the inertia groups in E_U. These depend on a choice of points x'_i over x_i in the normalization of X in L̄, so they are defined up to conjugacy. The formula reads
  E_X^{L̄} ≃ E_U^{L̄} / (closed normal subgroup generated by the I_{x_i}, i ∈ I).
This is the standard consequence of Zariski–Nagata purity for regular X. Removing the parts of Z of codimension ≥ 2 does not change π_1. For the divisorial part, a cover of U extends étale over X exactly when it is unramified at the generic points x_i. The symbol written 'E𝒢_L^{L̄}' links this to the quotient E_𝐋 of the previous page: the part 'universally given' by the compactifications. That quotient classifies the étale L-algebras that extend over (regular) compact models.

Formula (24): Gal(L̄/L) = E_L^{L̄} ≃ lim_U E_U^{L̄}, the projective limit over regular, and if one wishes affine, models U. This is the usual fact that the generic point is the limit of its open neighbourhoods (SGA 1 V). Formula (25) is the geometric (over K̄) version: Π_{L/K}^{L̄} ≃ lim Π_{U/K}.

The question raised. How can one describe the E_U (and E_L) in terms of local data? Grothendieck begins with the local situation at a divisor. Take a discrete valuation ring V of L containing K, a 'germ of model' of L/K at a codimension-1 point, i.e. at the generic point of a divisor. Let x be the closed point of S = Spec V.

The next page carries this on:
- A point x' over x gives a decomposition group N_{x'} and an inertia group I_{x'}.
- N/I is identified with the Galois group of k(x'), a field of transcendence degree n-1 over K.
- Via Kummer theory in characteristic 0, I ≅ T(L̄) ≅ T(K̄) = Ẑ(1).
- The henselization Ṽ gives a local field L̃_x and a homomorphism E_{Ũ_x} → E_L, well defined up to conjugacy.

The aim is a 'local-to-global' description of E_L and E_U by divisorial decomposition and inertia subgroups. This is the program later realized in birational anabelian geometry.
errors: (23) is valid only with X regular (or at least pure, e.g. regular in codim ≤ 2 near Z). It needs the closed normal subgroup generated by all conjugates of the inertia groups. The page says 'invariant' (normal), so this is essentially stated correctly, but the regularity hypothesis is only implicit.
The left side of (23) is written E_x with a lowercase-looking x; it must mean E_X for the compactification X, not the point x.
Notation drifts between E and Π, and between plain and barred superscripts L / L̄, in (23)–(25). (25) is the geometric-fundamental-group analogue of (24), obtained by taking kernels over Gal(K̄/K).
Next page: the identification I ≅ T(K̄) via Kummer requires characteristic 0, or restriction to the tame/prime-to-p part. The margin note there acknowledges this.

ideas.what: π_1 of a regular compactification as the quotient of π_1 of the open part by the normal subgroup generated by divisorial inertia
ideas.modern_name: Zariski–Nagata purity / Abhyankar-type description of π_1(X) from π_1(U)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. V and X (purity theorem X.3.1–3.4), SGA 2

ideas.what: Gal(L̄/L) as the projective limit of π_1 of the regular models of L/K, and similarly for geometric fundamental groups
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the generic point as a limit over models

ideas.what: Studying Gal(L̄/L), as an extension of Gal(K̄/K), via the decomposition and inertia groups of divisorial discrete valuations (germs of models at codimension-1 points), with inertia ≅ Ẑ(1)
ideas.modern_name: divisorial decomposition/inertia groups; local theory of birational anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pop (birational anabelian geometry, 1990s); Grothendieck's program in Esquisse/letter to Faltings
ideas.where_published: Birational anabelian philosophy is sketched in the Letter to Faltings (1983) and Esquisse (1984); the detailed 'Longue Marche' notes were not published by him.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the program of describing E_U and E_L = Gal(L̄/L) through the divisorial decomposition/inertia groups of germs of models. He also sets up recovering the 'compact' quotients E_X by killing those inertia groups. This is an early, explicit form of the local theory later developed by Pop and others (group-theoretic recognition of divisorial inertia). The page itself only poses the question and begins the local setup, so it is not new to specialists.
missed.quote: Comment décrire ... les E_U^{L̄} ? E_L^{L̄} ? ... (correspondant à un "germe de modèle" de L/K, au voisinage d'un pt de codim 1 i.e. du pt génér. d'un diviseur)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents the birational anabelian setup in Grothendieck's own notes. Mathematically it adds nothing beyond what is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material: purity, limits over models, and the decomposition/inertia groups of a DVR. It is used as setup for the known birational anabelian program. The only interest is historical, in seeing the setup in Grothendieck's notes.
transcription_corrections: In (23), the quotient reads '/ ss-groupe fermé invariant engendré par les I_{x_i} (i∈I)' (closed normal subgroup), not 'Π-groupe fondamental'.
The left side of (23) is E_X^{L̄} (X = compactification); the barred-L superscript was overwritten.
'Notons que E_L^{L̄} est la limite projective des E_U^{L̄}, pour des modèles réguliers (affines si on y tient) variables' — the reading is essentially correct.

'Considérons le cas de type où K' should probably read along the lines of 'Considérons ... un anneau de valuation discrète V de corps L, contenant K (correspondant à un "germe de modèle" ...)'. The insertion 'de-, V' is likely 'd.v.r. V'.
'considérons le corps fermé x' should be 'le point fermé x de S = Spec(V)'.
The 'Pour H' reading is doubtful; the underlined symbol may be Π or a section label.

The diagonal margin note is largely illegible in the transcription. It appears to say that in what follows K is taken provisionally in a certain form, with a later more general ('généralisé') setting involving separably closed/singular situations. The current transcription of it is unreliable.
